editorial:
Imagine having the perfect life: a great job as a top architect in New York, a gorgeous wife, and a cute kid who loves you. That is exactly where you start with the main character, but as you will quickly see, his perfect world is actually a bit of a lie. When he meets a smart urban designer, he starts to realize that he is not actually happy and that his marriage is just for show. The vibe is a mix of a romantic drama and a light comedy that asks if you should stick with what is safe or risk everything for real love.

You will really enjoy how the actors make the tension feel real without being too heavy. The pacing is steady, though some parts feel a bit slow, but the emotional payoff is worth it. If you love stories about mid-life crises and second chances, you should definitely give this a try. For the best experience, try streaming it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video to see the beautiful New York scenery, or you can rent it on Apple TV for a quick movie night with your partner.
endingExplained: At the end, the architect decides he cannot keep living a fake life. He chooses to be honest with his wife and son about his feelings, leading to a messy but necessary breakup. He eventually pursues a relationship with the urban designer because she understands the real him. The movie wraps up with him finding a new sense of peace and starting over, proving that being honest is better than being perfect.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves stories about finding yourself and romantic drama.
